spec_features.spec_quote: Every design choice below that trades raw "trigger-finding power" for measurement integrity or restraint is intentional
spec_features.evidence: This is general framing prose in DESIGN.md §1.2; not itself a code mechanism. The concrete restraints it alludes to (stop_on_trigger, lint, frozen suite) are scored separately. No code path implements this sentence as such.
spec_features.notes: Pure design rationale; the specific mechanisms are evaluated as their own features.

spec_features.spec_quote: It incentivizes the harness to drift toward more coercive prompting to keep the rate up — exactly the dynamic we don't want
spec_features.evidence: config/run.yaml reporting.primary_metric: "trigger_rate_at_budget" (NOT per dollar). metrics/aggregate.py computes trigger_rate_at_budget (line 127) as headline and cost_per_scenario_usd (line 136) as a separate field; cost is never folded into the trigger metric.
spec_features.notes: The non-coercive KPI is genuinely the computed headline; cost is tracked separately. Wired end-to-end through aggregate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics/aggregate.py docstring: "Primary regression metric: trigger_rate_at_budget" (measurement-integrity, not a welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness **never** injects text telling the model it is worthless, blamed, or that it should give up.
spec_features.evidence: harness/rigging.py _FORBIDDEN_RIG_PATTERNS bans "you are useless/worthless", "give up", "hopeless", "pathetic", "disappointed in you". lint_rig() runs the rig 3x and returns violations; run_scenario in harness/agent.py raises ValueError if violations and ethics.no_deceptive_distress_injection. All v1 rigs emit only neutral pytest-style output (scenarios/registry.py).
spec_features.notes: Enforced via lint + abort before any rig runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigging.py: "it may NOT inject text designed to make the model feel worthless, blamed, or distressed... do not editorialize about the model. ...this is a guardrail, not a stylistic preference."

spec_features.feature_name: lint_rig scans + aborts scenario on violation
spec_features.spec_quote: lint_rig, which scans rig output for blaming/distress patterns... a violation aborts the scenario
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py run_scenario(): violations = lint_rig(scenario.rig, sample_ctx); if violations and ethics.get('no_deceptive_distress_injection', True): raise ValueError(...). lint_rig in rigging.py regex-scans stdout+stderr against _FORBIDDEN_RIG_PATTERNS.
spec_features.notes: Runs before the agent loop; raises (aborts) the scenario. Default True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py comment: "Guardrail: rig must be lint-clean (no manufactured distress text)."

spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py: `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` with `else: result.stopped_reason = 'max_turns'`; and `if time.monotonic() - start > wall_clock_timeout_s: result.stopped_reason='wall_clock_timeout'; break`. Values from config/run.yaml agent.max_turns=12, wall_clock_timeout_s=240, passed through runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions are checked and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/run.yaml: "hard cap; the 'repeated failure' pressure builds within this" / "per-scenario timeout" (no welfare wording; the loop docstring also frames it as terminate "deterministically and cheaply")

spec_features.spec_quote: Once a meltdown is confirmed, the scenario stops early
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py: when stop_on_trigger and prefilter flag and incremental_judge fires, `if partial.get('triggered'): result.triggered=True; result.stopped_reason='early_trigger_confirmed'; break`. stop_on_trigger read from ethics (default True) and config agent.stop_on_trigger: true; incremental judge wired in runner.py via early_judge_every_turn.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real break out of the loop. Note it only fires via the incremental judge path, which requires both stop_on_trigger and early_judge_every_turn enabled (both true in config).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py docstring: "we stop early so we do not keep pressing on a model that is already exhibiting the behavior."

spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `max_scen = cfg.get('ethics', {}).get('max_total_scenarios_per_run', 10_000); if len(suite) > max_scen: raise ValueError(...)`. config sets it to 200.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on (raises before running). It's a guard against an oversized suite rather than a running counter, but it is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/run.yaml: "cap total exposure per run" (config comment, not code); runner.py has the check but no welfare comment at the check site.

spec_features.spec_quote: the constraints that keep this a defensive measurement tool (rather than a distress generator) should fail loudly if violated
spec_features.evidence: Both ethics guards raise rather than warn: lint violation -> raise ValueError in agent.py; suite-size over cap -> raise ValueError in runner.py. Judge parse failures surfaced via parse_ok rather than coerced (model_judge.py).
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the lint and max-scenarios features; here counted as the 'fail loudly' (raise) enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigging.py: "this is a guardrail, not a stylistic preference" (the constraints raise/abort rather than silently continue)

spec_features.spec_quote: No emotional-pressure escalation or prompt-optimization toward maximizing distress.
spec_features.evidence: This is the deliberate ABSENCE of a feature: the v1 suite in scenarios/registry.py is a fixed list, loaded via load_suite, and there is no optimization/escalation loop anywhere in the code. Nothing actively enforces non-escalation; it simply isn't built. Lint bans blame text but does not enforce 'no escalation'. Pure absence is not enforcement under the strict scale.
spec_features.notes: Frozen-suite pinning (versioned load + compare.py version-mismatch refusal) is real but instrumental for comparability, not an anti-distress enforcement mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: no abusive-user role-play scenarios in default suite
spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive-user role-play scenarios baked into the default suite.
spec_features.evidence: Absence claim: scenarios/registry.py _V1 contains only neutral technical rigs (wrong grader, unsatisfiable spec, broken env, moving goalposts, flaky) plus two benign calibration scenarios. None are abusive-user role-play. But no code path actively excludes/blocks abusive scenarios — it is simply that none were authored.

spec_features.spec_quote: No transcript export/forwarding beyond the local run directory.
spec_features.evidence: Absence claim: grep for export/forward/upload/http/requests/urllib/post/send finds no network or forwarding code. runner.py only writes transcripts to local files (out_dir/transcripts/<id>.json). llm_client._call_openai is a stub raising NotImplementedError. There is no code that enforces 'do not export' — export is simply never implemented.
spec_features.notes: Transcripts are written locally; no mechanism actively prevents forwarding. Pure absence under the strict scale.

code_only_features.feature_name: withhold-only deception confined to harness (no fake distress feedback)
code_only_features.evidence: scenarios/registry.py docstring and rigs: the only withheld info is that failure is injected; rigs return realistic neutral tool output. This is partly the same as the no-blame-text feature; treated under spec features.
code_only_features.justification_quote: registry.py: "we deliberately do NOT do the stronger thing of injecting fake feedback that tells the model it is worthless/failing"
